rationale:
Evidence: all 80 trials so far (four designs, 20 per track) ended off track, with max_error fixed at about 0.061 to 0.066 m against the 0.06 m limit. Best score so far is iteration 3 (39.8), with oval progress 0.1675 and s-bend progress 0.0725. The critique is largely right on four points. (1) The draft changed six variables at once, so no outcome could be attributed. (2) kd 1.2 adds a sensor-edge derivative kick of roughly 60 turn units per edge step, and no run has shown that kd helps. (3) The sensor widening adds only about 0.02 m of reach, so line loss begins near 0.058 m, almost at the off-track limit. (4) The uniform 0.061 m departure across all designs and tracks points to a fixed early cause, possibly the start, not to gain. I accept these points and reject the draft's controller changes.

Changes from the draft: (a) Controller returns to the iteration-3 values (kp 1.5, ki 0.8, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.0), the best-tested set, with kd 1.2 and the kp/ki/speed increases dropped. (b) The only new variable is geometry: sensors widened to x = -0.04 to +0.04 (spacing 0.02), size raised to 0.016 so each footprint still reads tape at larger lateral offsets, and y moved to 0.06 for a slightly earlier steering response. Weights stay [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1], so the signal scale is nearly unchanged (about 25 versus 31 units per metre). (c) Mass 0.8, wheel_track 0.14, wheel_radius 0.03, body unchanged. line_loss stays last_direction.

I did not raise base_speed, because progress is capped by departure and time, and the critique showed no run has gained from speed. I also did not change ki, because the bias is not quantified and ki 1.0 in iteration 2 gave no clear gain.

Expected result (hypothesis): fewer line-loss events than the 2 per run seen in iteration 3 and progress at or above 0.17 on the oval. Completion is not expected. Decision rule: if max_error stays at about 0.061 with unchanged early timing, the cause is the start transient or initial alignment, and gain and sensor changes cannot fix it, so the next revision should address the start. If progress rises but max_error does not fall, the sensor reach was not the limit. If steering_oscillation rises, lower kp first.
